title: Layered Material Blending System with Time Control
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a layered material blending system with time-based animation control on a central sphere.

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x111118). Perspective camera at (0, 0, 4) looking at origin.
- One ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.4) and one directional light (0xffffff, intensity 1.0) at position (3, 5, 4).
- A single sphere (radius 1.2, 64x64 segments) centered at origin, slowly rotating on Y axis (0.15 rad/s).
- The sphere uses a custom ShaderMaterial that blends up to 4 material layers.

## Material Layers
Define exactly 4 layers, each with a base color, roughness, and metalness:
- Layer 0 'Base': color (0.8, 0.2, 0.1), roughness 0.9, metalness 0.0
- Layer 1 'Metal': color (0.9, 0.9, 0.95), roughness 0.15, metalness 1.0
- Layer 2 'Glow': color (0.1, 0.8, 0.4), roughness 0.5, metalness 0.3
- Layer 3 'Glass': color (0.3, 0.5, 0.9), roughness 0.05, metalness 0.6

Each layer has a blend weight (0.0 to 1.0). Initially: Layer 0 = 1.0, Layers 1-3 = 0.0.
The final material properties are computed as weighted averages: finalColor = sum(layer[i].color * weight[i]) / sum(weight[i]), same for roughness and metalness. If total weight is 0, use Layer 0 defaults.

## Time Control System
- A global timeline from 0.0 to 10.0 seconds.
- The timeline has keyframes that define target blend weights at specific times:
  - t=0.0: weights [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
  - t=2.5: weights [0.5, 0.5, 0.0, 0.0]
  - t=5.0: weights [0.0, 0.3, 0.7, 0.0]
  - t=7.5: weights [0.0, 0.0, 0.3, 0.7]
  - t=10.0: weights [0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25]
- Between keyframes, weights are linearly interpolated.
- A Play/Pause button toggles timeline playback. Playback speed is 1x real-time.
- A timeline slider (range input, id='timelineSlider') allows scrubbing to any point. When scrubbing, playback pauses automatically.
- A speed control dropdown (id='speedSelect') with options: 0.5x, 1x, 2x. Default 1x.

## User Interactions
- Click on the sphere to cycle through a 'solo mode': Off -> Solo Layer 0 -> Solo Layer 1 -> Solo Layer 2 -> Solo Layer 3 -> Off. In solo mode, only the soloed layer's weight is used (set to 1.0, others to 0.0), overriding the timeline. Display current solo state in HUD.
- Press keys 1-4 to manually toggle individual layer visibility (enabled/disabled). Disabled layers have their weight forced to 0. This is independent of solo mode. All layers start enabled.
- Press Space to toggle Play/Pause.
- Press R to reset timeline to t=0 and stop playback.
- Press S to take a snapshot: store the current blended color, roughness, metalness, and time into a snapshots array (max 5, FIFO).

## HUD / UI
- Top-left: current time (2 decimal places), playback state (Playing/Paused), speed.
- Top-right: for each layer show name, current weight (2 decimals), enabled/disabled status.
- Bottom: timeline slider spanning full width, speed dropdown, Play/Pause button (id='playPauseBtn'), Reset button (id='resetBtn'), Snapshot button (id='snapshotBtn').
- Below slider: show snapshot count.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame with:
- currentTime: number (0-10)
- isPlaying: boolean
- playbackSpeed: number
- layerWeights: [number, number, number, number] (the raw interpolated weights before solo/enable overrides)
- effectiveWeights: [number, number, number, number] (actual weights after solo/enable overrides)
- layerEnabled: [boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean]
- soloMode: number (-1 for off, 0-3 for soloed layer index)
- blendedColor: {r, g, b} (0-1 range, the final computed color)
- blendedRoughness: number
- blendedMetalness: number
- snapshots: array of {time, color:{r,g,b}, roughness, metalness}
- snapshotCount: number
- sphereRotationY: number (current Y rotation in radians)
- totalWeight: number (sum of effective weights)
- frameCount: number (incremented each frame)
physics_constraints: Blend weights must be clamped to [0,1]. Effective weights must sum to > 0 when computing averages (fallback to Layer 0 defaults). Blended color channels must be in [0,1]. Roughness in [0,1]. Metalness in [0,1]. Timeline clamped to [0,10]. Linear interpolation between keyframes must be exact. Sphere rotation must be continuous and NaN-free.
